title: Storage bandwidth glitch + scheduling backlog — retrospective (draft)
content:
Summary:

This doc captures notes from the Nov 1–2, 2025 incident where a transient storage-bandwidth saturation on a subset of GPU node pools triggered prolonged pod start latency and a scheduler backlog. The cluster experienced a cascading scheduling delay across multiple availability zones for ~45 minutes, causing degraded API latency and several customer-facing request timeouts.

Primary symptoms observed:
- Spike in pod Pending time (p95 from ~10s -> ~180s) for batch-worker and model-load jobs.
- node-exporter / node-level iops/bandwidth metrics showed short bursts where host-side NVMe bandwidth exceeded usual envelope (20–40s bursts).
- kubelet started reporting image pull + container start stalls and increased eviction churn (disk pressure heuristics oscillating).
- Scheduler logs show exponential increase in backoff and queue depth; master CPU p95 increased due to scheduling churn.
- Some nodes reported transient Docker/containerd errors: "backoff pulling image" then later "failed to create container: device busy" in logs.

Impact scope:
- Scope: three GPU node pools (gpu-prod-a, gpu-prod-b, gpu-prod-c) across two AZs.
- Surface-level: ~120 pods delayed, ~8 customer routes hit 5xx due to downstream timeouts.
- Duration: active anomaly ~45 minutes, subsequent remediation and rollout ~2.5 hours.

Timeline (high-level):
- 2025-11-01 21:02 UTC — alert: node-exporter bandwidth alert firing for gpu-prod-a (one node).
- 21:04 UTC — scheduler p95 pod pending > 60s alert.
- 21:04–21:15 UTC — incident response: SRE oncall (Ethan) triaged; noticed correlated host bandwidth spikes.
- 21:10 UTC — mitigations: evacuated two most-affected nodes (cordon+drain) -> started moving pods into less-saturated pools.
- 21:20 UTC — discovered recent daemonset upgrade (driver-update) had initiated bulk image pulls on some nodes ~20:56 UTC; this coincided with bandwidth bursts.
- 21:30 UTC — rolling restart of the driver daemonset paused and switched to rate-limited pulls.
- 21:42 UTC — pod pending p95 returned to ~15s.
- 23:30 UTC — post-incident checks completed, formal follow-ups documented.

Root-cause hypothesis (current):
1) Mass parallel image pulls and driver artifact fetches (from the driver daemonset rollout) produced short-lived host-level storage/network bandwidth saturation on nodes sharing the same NIC path to backend storage (host-attached NVMe + local daemon counters).
2) Kubelet image-pull and container creation operations blocked on filesystem I/O, which in turn increased container create latency and pushed pods into Pending while scheduler waited for capacity.
3) Some kubelet eviction heuristics reacted to transient I/O anomalies, toggling diskPressure and causing extra churn (pods recreated/evicted) and further increasing scheduler load.
4) The rollout had no global rate limit or awareness of storage bandwidth, so several nodes hit the same backend concurrently.

Evidence for hypothesis:
- node-exporter graphs: bandwidth spikes align with daemonset rollout window (driver artifacts ~2–4GB per node).
- kubelet logs: repeated "i/o timeout" and "device busy" around containerd/imagepull timestamps.
- audit of ClusterOps PR: the daemonset change included image -> from new registry mirror; no rate-limiting added.
- nodes under saturation show disk scheduler queue growth and soft requeue of container creation tasks.

Mitigations performed during incident:
- Immediate: cordon+drain top 2 saturated nodes to stop scheduling onto them and reduce in-flight pulls.
- Paused the daemonset rollout and reverted the container image tag for the driver rollout.
- Applied temporary QoS on pull traffic by adjusting mirroring endpoint (forced some pulls to different mirror).
- Emergency: increased kube-scheduler QPS limit temporarily to reduce scheduling latency from controller loops (careful: this is a tactical tweak).

Post-incident action items (short-term):
- Add rate-limiting to future daemonset rollouts that touch >10% of nodes of a given pool (PR: infra-ops #142).
- Add an admission check in our rollout tool to estimate total bytes to be pulled per node pool and abort if > X GiB in N minutes.
- Improve observability: create a composite alert that correlates host IO bandwidth bursts with kubelet image-pull errors and scheduler pending p95.
- Adjust kubelet eviction sensitivity for short I/O spikes: evaluate raising diskPressure threshold or adding hysteresis to avoid rapid toggling.
- Document a node-pooling guideline: avoid updating large drivers on full pools at once—use staggered waves by AZ and by NIC-path tag.

Runbook / playbook additions (draft steps):
- Detection: alert on (node.bandwidth_write_p95 > threshold AND kubelet.image_pull_errors > N in 1m) OR scheduler.pending_p95 > 60s.
- Immediate triage steps:
  1) Check daemonset rollouts (kubectl -n infra get ds driver-daemonset -o wide) and find rollout start time.
  2) Query node-exporter: top bandwidth nodes in last 10m (promQL provided below).
  3) If <5% nodes affected, cordon+drain the top 2 and scale up ephemeral nodes into a different pool.
  4) Pause the rollout (kubectl rollout pause) and set imagePullPolicy to not trigger re-pull as temporary step.
  5) If many nodes affected, stop the rollout globally and open ops channel with SRE lead.
- Recovery validation: ensure kubelet metrics return to baseline (imagePullErrors ~0, pending_p95 < 20s) and no sustained evictions.

Useful commands / promql / logs (notes to self):
- promql examples:
  - top bandwidth nodes: topk(10, node_network_receive_bytes_total{device!~"lo"}[1m])
  - kubelet image pull errors: sum(rate(container_runtime_operations_errors_total{operation="pull"}[1m])) by (node)
  - pending p95: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(kube_pod_container_status_waiting_total[5m])) by (le))
- useful kubectl snippets:
  - kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector=status.phase=Pending -n prod
  - kubectl describe node <node> | egrep -A3 "Non-terminated Pods|Conditions"
  - journalctl -u kubelet -o short-precise | sed -n 'T,;p' | grep -i pull

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why did some nodes show higher host-bandwidth despite identical instance types and storage config? (Possibility: NIC path / rack-level contention or host-local background process such as backup jobs.)
- Did any third-party monitoring agent cause extra read on disk (we saw version bump of backup-agent in same timeframe)? Need to correlate package manager activity on nodes.
- Confirm whether device-driver post-install scripts invoked additional rsync/copy steps on nodes (we saw small copies recorded).

Longer-term proposals:
- Implement cluster-level "bulk-pull guardrails" in rollout system — track aggregate bytes being pulled per pool and throttle.
- Add kernel-level IO latency SLO dashboards per node-pool and expose to release engineers as preflight check.
- Introduce a "stagger-mode" in daemonset controller for infra-critical daemons (stagger_by: az and stride=3).
- Revisit kubelet eviction thresholds and add a disk-io hysteresis metric to avoid oscillation on <1m spikes.

Notes / other artifacts discovered during postmortem:
- Related ticket: ENGSRE-2147 (driver rollout investigation).
- PR: infra-monitoring #142 adds the composite alert (draft).
- Slack channel: #sre-incident-2147 (contains timeline and command history).

Retro / learnings (short):
- Rolling upgrades that touch storage-heavy artifacts are a higher risk than pure config changes — treat them like DB migrations and apply stricter guardrails.
- Observability gaps made it slower to correlate pulls -> IO spikes -> kubelet errors; composite alerts and quick query templates would have shortened MTTR by ~10–15 minutes.
- Kubelet eviction heuristics are sensitive to bursty IO; adding hysteresis reduces reactive churn and scheduler pressure.

Next steps owner and target dates:
- infra-ops: add rate-limit check + abort on rollout (owner: Priya Nair) — target 2025-11-14.
- monitoring: add composite alert + dashboard (owner: Lukas Meyer) — target 2025-11-10.
- kubelet tuning investigation and lab testing (owner: SRE performance team / Sofia Ramos) — target 2025-12-01.

Notes to self: preserve raw kubelet journals and node-exporter samples from the incident window in artifacts/ENGSRE-2147/raw for 90 days. Also tag the driver daemonset PR with this incident so release engineers see the link when changing images in the future.

-- Ethan Z. (oncall)
